domain: Social Ontology / Medical Classification / Rights Frameworks
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested category kernel where 'woman' and 'female' are read either as sex-defined-by-biology or gender-defined-by-identity. Each reading emits constraints with different membership criteria and victim sets. The contest operates across medical classification, legal recognition, spatial access rights, and institutional policy domains.

key_entities: NIH Office of Women's Health Research (institutional site of definitional conflict in 1990s)
Declaration on Women's Sex-Based Rights (2019 advocacy framework, 30K+ signatories)
Gender identity rights advocates (framework prioritizing self-identification)
Sex-based rights advocates (framework prioritizing biological classification)
Intersex individuals (biological edge case challenging binary)
Transgender women (population whose category membership differs by reading)
Federal agencies (enforcement bodies for sex-based vs gender-based frameworks)
key_claims: Sex is biological, binary, immutable, observable (sex-based reading axiom)
Gender identity is self-determined, central to personhood, takes precedence over sex (gender-identity reading axiom)
Inclusion of trans women in 'women' category constitutes sex-based discrimination (sex-based framework claim)
Exclusion of trans women from 'women' category constitutes gender identity discrimination (gender-identity framework claim)
Both perspectives can coexist with diversity as default (proposed resolution)
Conflation of sex and gender has pitted biology against culture (meta-critique)
key_tensions: Binary biological classification vs spectrum of gender identities (ontological)
Sex-based spatial access vs gender-identity spatial access (women's spaces, prisons, sports)
Biological researchers vs behavioral scholars at NIH (disciplinary epistemology)
Material consequences of sexed bodies vs social construction of gender (paradox of gender)
key_mechanisms: Legal sex classification systems (state enforcement of category membership)
Self-identification protocols (administrative mechanism for gender identity recognition)
Single-sex space access policies (institutional gatekeeping mechanism)
key_absences: Intersex individuals' position in both frameworks (biological edge case largely unaddressed)
Non-binary identities' relationship to sex-based protections (neither framework fully accounts)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sex-biology reading holds category membership is observer-independent biological fact; gender-identity reading holds category membership is subject-dependent self-identification. No single framework can hold both 'membership is independent of subject's claim' and 'membership is constituted by subject's claim' as simultaneously true for the same category.

omegas.description: Intersex individuals (1.7% of population) destabilize both readings: sex-biology reading cannot cleanly classify them; gender-identity reading does not address their biological distinctiveness. Neither framework provides adequate protection. Deferred axis medical_classification_instability.

Non-binary identities are structurally erased by both readings: sex-biology reading has no category for them; gender-identity reading focuses on binary trans identities. A third reading (non-binary ontology) may be required.

Is intersectional_coexistence_reading a viable scaffold or a rhetorical evasion? Dual-track systems exist in some jurisdictions but face administrative collapse under adversarial pressure. Empirical test: do dual-track systems survive legal challenge?

Both readings claim victim status for their excluded population. Is this symmetrical (equal harms) or asymmetrical (one population faces greater material harm)? Requires empirical harm measurement, not axiom comparison.

What grounds interpretive authority over the category kernel? Sex-biology reading appeals to scientific observation (but science cannot derive 'ought' from 'is'); gender-identity reading appeals to phenomenological experience (but subjective experience cannot bind others). Neither authority structure is self-legitimating.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition applied correctly: three readings selected (two axiom-contradictory core readings + one downstream synthesis node). Intersex edge case and non-binary erasure documented as omegas. Disciplinary epistemology captured in authority_grounding rather than separate axis.
